body:
**Claude finished @spenes's task in 3m 1s** —— [View job](https://github.com/snowplow-incubator/snowplow-identities/actions/runs/34597160956)

---
### Review: `merge_graph_size_max` gauge → sampled metric

- [x] Read the PR diff
- [x] Inspect the metrics `Sample` / flush pipeline
- [x] Check for stale references to `merge_graph_size_max`
- [x] Static analysis of the new wiring
- [x] Post review

The direction is right: a last-value gauge sampled at the flush boundary genuinely under-reports interval peaks, and routing the per-batch peak through `AddSample` so `Flush` (`pkg/metrics/metrics.go:577-581`) derives `_max` gives a true interval max. Keeping the constant named `merge_graph_size` so the derived series is still called `merge_graph_size_max` is a nice touch — the emitted name survives.

Four things worth addressing before merge.

---

#### 1. Merge-free batches record a `0` sample, flattening the mean and pinning `_min` to zero

`pkg/service/batch_processor.go:717-719` samples on every `planOperations` call whenever `max_merges` is enabled, but `ctx.maxGraphSize` is only ever written inside `planMergeOrDowngrade` (`batch_processor.go:792-794`). A batch that plans only CREATE/LINK operations leaves it at its zero value, so a `0` is sampled.

Under the old gauge this was harmless — only the last value mattered, and consumers were told to read the max. Now the new comment advertises the mean and `_min` as products of this metric (`pkg/metrics/metrics.go:298-300`), and both are dominated by merge-free batches: `merge_graph_size_min` will be `0` in essentially every interval, and `merge_graph_size` (the mean) is a mean over batches-that-merged plus batches-that-didn't, which measures merge frequency more than graph size. `_max` is unaffected, which is the series the alarms use, but two of the three advertised series are noise.

```go
if config.MergeLimitEnabled(bp.maxMerges) && bp.metrics.MergeGraphSize != nil && ctx.maxGraphSize > 0 {
	bp.metrics.MergeGraphSize(ctx.maxGraphSize)
}
```

Also worth stating in the comment that the mean/min are over **per-batch peaks**, not over graph sizes — with one sample per batch they can't be anything else, and a reader seeing `merge_graph_size` will assume otherwise. (Sampling each `graphSize` at `batch_processor.go:791` would give a real distribution, but that's up to 4000 mutex-guarded `AddSample` calls per batch on the hot planning path — the per-batch peak is the right trade-off; it just needs to be documented as such.) [Fix this →](https://claude.ai/code?q=On%20branch%20fiddle%2F7172e65b061629ab%2C%20in%20pkg%2Fservice%2Fbatch_processor.go%20lines%20717-719%3A%20the%20MergeGraphSize%20sample%20is%20recorded%20on%20every%20planOperations%20call%2C%20so%20batches%20that%20plan%20no%20merges%20record%20a%20zero%20sample%20%28ctx.maxGraphSize%20is%20only%20written%20in%20planMergeOrDowngrade%29.%20Add%20a%20ctx.maxGraphSize%20%3E%200%20condition%20so%20merge-free%20batches%20do%20not%20drag%20the%20derived%20mean%20down%20and%20pin%20merge_graph_size_min%20to%20zero.%20Also%20amend%20the%20doc%20comment%20in%20pkg%2Fmetrics%2Fmetrics.go%20around%20line%20296%20to%20say%20the%20mean%20and%20_min%20are%20over%20per-batch%20peaks%2C%20not%20over%20individual%20graph%20sizes.&repo=snowplow-incubator/snowplow-identities)

#### 2. `Sampled` has no constructor, so both wiring sites hand-roll the same closure

`pkg/metrics/metrics.go:363` adds `type Sampled func(value int)`, but the `Metrics` interface gains no factory for it, unlike `Counter(name) Counted`, `Gauge(name) Gauged` and `TimingFunc(name) Timed`. The result is the identical adapter duplicated at `cmd/serve.go:240` and `pkg/idtest/idtest.go:395`:

```go
MergeGraphSize: func(v int) { metrics.Sample(mx.MergeGraphSize, float64(v)) },
```

Every future sampled metric will copy that line into both files, and the `int → float64 → float32` conversion chain lives at the call site rather than in the sink. Adding `Sampler(name string) Sampled` to the interface and `HashiMetrics` keeps the new type consistent with the three that precede it and reduces the two call sites to `metrics.Sampler(mx.MergeGraphSize)`. [Fix this →](https://claude.ai/code?q=On%20branch%20fiddle%2F7172e65b061629ab%3A%20the%20new%20mx.Sampled%20type%20in%20pkg%2Fmetrics%2Fmetrics.go%20line%20363%20has%20no%20constructor%20on%20the%20Metrics%20interface%2C%20unlike%20Counter%2FGauge%2FTimingFunc%2C%20so%20cmd%2Fserve.go%20line%20240%20and%20pkg%2Fidtest%2Fidtest.go%20line%20395%20each%20hand-roll%20the%20same%20closure.%20Add%20Sampler%28name%20string%29%20Sampled%20to%20the%20Metrics%20interface%20and%20implement%20it%20on%20HashiMetrics%20%28wrapping%20Sample%20with%20the%20int-to-float64%20conversion%29%2C%20then%20use%20metrics.Sampler%28mx.MergeGraphSize%29%20at%20both%20wiring%20sites.&repo=snowplow-incubator/snowplow-identities)

#### 3. The name survives but the statsd metric *type* changes — downstream dashboards break silently

`merge_graph_size_max` used to reach the sink via `SetGaugeWithLabels` (`|g` packets); it now goes out via `AddSampleWithLabels` (`pkg/metrics/metrics.go:580`), which the DogStatsD sink emits as a timing (`|ms`). In Datadog that turns the series into the `merge_graph_size_max.avg` / `.max` / `.median` family, so any existing monitor or panel querying the plain gauge `merge_graph_size_max` goes to *no data* rather than erroring — the worst failure mode for a near-cap alarm.

Nothing in the repo references `merge_graph_size` (I grepped: no dashboard JSON, no runbook scenario), so those definitions live outside it and this PR can't fix them. Please call the type change out in the PR description so whoever owns the Grafana/Datadog side updates the queries. Two secondary consequences of the same switch: the value is now typed as milliseconds by the receiver even though it counts merges, and `Flush`'s log line formats samples with a hard-coded `ms` suffix (`metrics.go:588`), so the log will read `merge_graph_size: count=1 min=3.000000ms`. Both match the existing `batch_request_size` precedent, so they're consistency notes, not regressions.

#### 4. Removal from `ServeGauges` drops the dormant-zero guarantee

`pkg/metrics/metrics.go:38-44` no longer registers the metric, so `Init()` (`metrics.go:599-608`) no longer re-emits it at zero each interval. Samples have no dormant equivalent — contrast `TestFlush_DormantCounterEmitsZero`. With #1 applied this is arguably the correct semantics (an interval with no merges *shouldn't* claim a graph size of 0), but it is a behavioural change: the series becomes sparse, and monitors configured to notify on missing data will start flapping during quiet periods. Worth one sentence in the PR body alongside #3.

---

#### Smaller notes

- **No test covers the new wiring.** Both `MergeGraphSize` and `MergeGraphNearCap` are nil-guarded at `batch_processor.go:717` and `:795`, so if the closure is ever dropped from `cmd/serve.go` the metric silently disappears with no failing test. `pkg/metrics/metrics_test.go:483` already proves `Sample` emits bare/`_min`/`_max`, so the gap is specifically the service→metrics wiring, which `pkg/idtest` is positioned to assert.
- **Comment accuracy.** I checked `effectiveGraphSize` (`batch_processor.go:815-821`) — it returns a merge count, so the retained `size = value + 1` sentence is still correct.
- `Gauged` and `Sampled` share an underlying type but are distinct named types, so they aren't mutually assignable — the type does buy real safety at the struct field.

#### Not verified

`go build ./...` and `go test` were blocked by this environment's permissions, so the review is static only. The four files are type-consistent as far as I can tell by reading — `mx.Sampled` is satisfied by both closures, and `MergeGraphSizeMax` has no remaining references anywhere in the tree.
 · branch [`fiddle/7172e65b061629ab`](https://github.com/snowplow-incubator/snowplow-identities/tree/fiddle/7172e65b061629ab)
